content.title: Ivisic twins helping fuel Illini postseason run
content.text: To subscribe, click here.HOUSTON — Tomislav Ivisic had an easy answer when the Illinois men’s basketball coaching staff asked if he wanted to play with twin brother Zvonimir.“It was a no-brainer,” he said. “I just said, ‘Of course, I think he’s a great basketball player. You guys do what you need to do, but he would love to come here. I would love him to be here.’”The move has paid off for the Illini, who are on the doorstep of their first Final Four appearance since 2005.The Ivisic brothers have been a big part of the equation, with Tomislav averaging 10.2 points and 5.7 rebounds in the starting lineup and Zvonimir contributing 6.7 points and 4.7 rebounds off the bench ahead of Saturday’s Elite Eight meeting against Iowa.“It’s been great so far,” Zvonimir said. “We’ve had a lot of fun together. I love playing with him, he loves playing with me. Connection is there and everything. It’s crazy for me to be on this stage with my brother.”Zvonimir started his college basketball career at Kentucky in 2023 before transferring to Arkansas for the 2024-25 season. He registered 13 points and six rebounds in a 90-77 loss to Illinois on Nov. 28, 2024, but went on to play a key role as the Razorbacks advanced to the Sweet 16.He frequently talked with his brother on FaceTime during that season, which was Tomislav’s first and Zvonimir’s second of college basketball. Tomislav started 31 of his 32 appearances with the Illini during his first season, in which he was classified as a junior.So Zvonimir knew plenty about Illinois — and life in Champaign-Urbana — before he entered the transfer portal prior to the 2025-26 season.“I already kind of knew how it is here,” Zvonimir said. “I heard a lot of great things about Champaign and this program. I’ve wanted to be with him since he came here.”Tomislav had already decided he’d be back at Illinois prior to Zvonimir’s decision — if he wasn’t playing professionally.“I knew one thing, that if I don’t go to the (NBA draft), I’m coming back here,” he said. “It was an easy decision. I liked the program. I like the coaches’ mentality, play hard. It’s all about winning here … it was an easy decision.”Forward Ben Humrichous quickly realized that Zvonimir would be a winning addition for the Illini.“Playing against (Zvonimir) last year was fun, but I knew the skill Z brought coming here to the University of Illinois and the asset that he would be to us,” Humrichous said. “So when I heard that we were getting a pair of twins, it was such a big deal to me.”That Tomislav stands at 7-foot-1 and Zvonimir eclipses him at 7-foot-2 has made Illinois one of the tallest college basketball teams in the country.And Tomislav is now on the doorstep of helping Illinois make program history.“I feel like I belong here,” he said. “They accepted me very well from the first moment. They only had one goal from the first day: Just work hard. Don’t take anything for granted. One game at a time, and we know that we’re good enough to be here. And we’re not done yet.”Forward Jake Davis made frequent appearances on those FaceTime calls between the Ivisic brothers. He’s been Tomislav’s roommate for the last two seasons.Zvonimir has roomed with Mihailo Petrovic this season but remains close with Tomislav and Davis.“Me and him kind of built a connection from day one,” Davis said. “We get along. We like a lot of the same things. And then when Z came here, he’s his twin, you know what I mean? So I treated him as my brother, and Z comes here and he’s his brother, so we’re all brothers.”Tomislav, for his part, has gotten used to having a roommate.“When I saw him for the first time in my room, I didn’t know I was going to have a roommate,” Tomislav said. “From that moment, we just clicked. He introduced me to America and American cultures, and we hang out a lot.”During practice before Illinois’ Sweet 16 win over Houston, coach Brad Underwood wore a pair of shoes that had flags from each of the five countries represented on the Illini’s roster.Tomislav has taught Davis plenty about his native Croatia, just as Davis helped him get up to speed on life in the United States.“I’ve learned a lot, I would say,” Davis said. “There’s so many things about the rest of the world you wouldn’t even know. He and a bunch of other guys (have) opened up to what it’s like overseas, what it’s like maybe somewhere outside of America. It’s been super informative.”Guard Kylan Boswell has an easy description of what the Ivisic twins are like away from the court. And how helpful they are on the court.“They’re goofballs. Silly guys,” Boswell said. “But having two twin towers back there for us defensively, and then on the offensive end, getting boards, making the right plays as a big. How well they both can shoot can stretch it for all of us.”Davis agrees that Tomislav is a bit more laid back away from basketball.“Behind the scenes, he’s not locked in whatsoever,” Davis said. “When it comes to basketball, he’s very serious, obviously. Takes care of his business. But outside of basketball, he’s very much, ‘Let’s go have fun. Let’s do what we want to do,’ (and) have a great time.”Tomislav didn’t partake in any ice cream following Thursday’s win against Houston, though many of his teammates did. He did, however, join in the water-gun fight that left the Illini locker room drenched.But his focus is back on Saturday’s Elite Eight matchup against the Hawkeyes, whom the Illini beat 75-69 on Jan. 11 in Iowa City.“Knowing what we work hard for all year,” he said. “It’s a huge achievement to be here in the Elite Eight, but we know that we could do better things than that. We’ve been practicing for this all year, and we’re not going to let the opportunity slide.” Joey Wright is a reporter covering prep and college sports for The News-Gazette and WDWS/WHMS/WKIO radio.
